name: Cortagen

lead: Cortagen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) is a four-amino-acid peptide made by Khavinson's group, modelled on the brain-cortex preparation Cortexin. Interest is in cognition and brain ageing rather than looks.

The chain runs from a brain-tissue peptide to support of neural ageing to cognitive wellbeing. Studies cover cell cultures, rodents and small reports, with changes in gene and interleukin-2 expression, sciatic nerve regeneration and free-radical processes. One Russian report compared Cortexin and Cortagen in chronic ischaemia.

paras: It is used in periodic courses within longevity peptide routines, often with other Khavinson peptides. Users describe expecting slow, general effects.
Human safety data are essentially absent from the published literature, and it is not an approved drug in Western countries.

angle.text: Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide modelled on Cortexin, used by longevity enthusiasts for brain ageing and cognition. It has been studied in cells and animals; appearance has not been studied.

lead: Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro, made by Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia from the amino-acid analysis of Cortexin, a natural brain-cortex peptide preparation [1]. It is one of the short synthetic peptide bioregulators the group proposes as tissue-specific regulators of ageing-related changes [1].

Published work consists of cell-culture, animal and small biochemical studies, many from the developers' laboratory. They examined gene expression in mouse heart [1], interleukin-2 expression [2][3], sciatic nerve regeneration [4] and free-radical processes [5]. One Russian report compared Cortexin and Cortagen in brain function in chronic ischaemia [6].
It is not an appearance product and no published trial in healthy people examines it.

paras: A microarray study in mice reported that Cortagen altered gene expression in heart tissue, which the authors framed as part of screening molecular targets of peptide bioregulators in ageing [1]. In rat and mouse cell systems, Cortagen had weaker immunomodulating effects than the related peptides Vilon and Epithalon: it produced no comitogenic effect on thymocytes [7] and a less pronounced effect on interleukin-2 mRNA in splenocytes [3], although in vivo work reported modulation of interleukin-2 expression in hypothalamic cells [2].

Other reports examined its effect on sciatic nerve regeneration [4], tissue-specific effects of peptides [8], free-radical processes [5], and lymphocyte chromatin and epigenetic markers in old cells [9][10]. A Russian paper compared Cortexin and Cortagen in functional and metabolic brain disorders in chronic ischaemia [6].
No studies found. The existing literature is limited to cell-culture, animal and chromatin work, plus one Russian-language report on brain ischaemia [6].
